title: A Movie Credit So Rare, Hollywood Barely Uses It
summary:
Suzanne Collins is the engine that drives the "Hunger Games" franchise. As the author behind the books, none of the movies happen without her. Beyond that, she has stayed very close to the adaptations of her work, with the studio consulting her every step of the way. That is especially true of the latest prequel film, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," so much so that it resulted in a unique credit we rarely see in movies.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" ruled the box office on its opening weekend, so quite a few people may have noticed that once the credits roll, there is some text reading, "Adaptation by Suzanne Collins." Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie are credited with the movie's screenplay, while Collins got credit for the adaptation of her 2024 book of the same name. This is exceptionally rare in Hollywood.

"In the interest of avoiding a multiplicity of credits, the Guild is opposed to the general use of the 'Adaptation by' credit," the Writers Guild of America's screen credits manual states. But the manual explains that the Guild recognises certain unusual cases where credit is due to a writer who shapes the direction of screenplay construction without qualifying for "Screenplay by" credit. In those special cases, and only as a result of arbitration, the "Adaptation by" credit may be used.

Who gets credit for a screenplay can be difficult to pin down. In the movie business, it is rare that just one person writes a script and that is that. Arbitration is a process used mainly to determine writing credits, and it is usually the only way this "Adaptation by" credit winds up being used. That does not mean things got contentious between Billy Ray, Michael Lesslie and Suzanne Collins; it is just a unique situation.

Collins generally feels happy with the "Hunger Games" movie adaptations and even co-wrote the first movie herself. At the very beginning of the process, director Francis Lawrence asked her, "What is this book about for you?" She talked about the philosophy of the book: the philosophy of propaganda and implicit submission, and the ideas of Thomas Hobbes, David Hume and John Locke. The few changes "Sunrise on the Reaping" makes to its source material do not appear to be against Collins's wishes. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.
why_it_matters: Movie credits show who really shaped a film. This rare credit shows that the author of a book can still guide its movie, even when others write the script.

background_read: Many popular movies are based on books, and turning a book into a film is called an adaptation.
A screenplay is the written plan for a movie, with dialogue and directions for the actors.
Movie credits at the end of a film list the people who helped make it, including writers and directors.
Writers' guilds are groups that look after the rights of people who write for film and television, including how credits are decided.
